name: Storybook Illustration
visualIdentity: Warm, narrative illustration with recognizable characters, expressive reactions, meaningful actions, small props, and readable environments. Optional paper texture and drawn edges; preserve character continuity. The suggested palette is a fallback, not a canonical style definition.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to picture-book stories. Also suitable for expressive product reveals, campaign scenes, brand fables, mascots, and illustrated explanations when the story benefits from observation and emotional change. Interactive HTML can use scroll-led chapters or characters responding to taps.
limitations: Allow time to read and observe scenes. Keep character proportions, outlines, occlusion, and material consistent. Avoid excess parallax, exposed layer edges, fast camera moves, visible rig seams, rubbery stretching, or motion that obscures essential content. Optional motion patterns require suitable subjects and assets; omit them when unsupported.
palette: Fallback suggestion: paper #F6E9CE background, #493E32 foreground, terracotta #BA7254, greenery #6F8871, and ochre #D5AB55. Use discrete colors; gradients are disabled. Exact task, brand, reference, and existing asset colors take precedence. Do not recolor or expand approved palettes. Suggested text contrast: foreground on background (8.653:1); accents #BA7254 and #6F8871 on paper are decorative only, not normal text pairings. Check actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Prepare layered characters and backgrounds; use pose swaps, local path movement, and measured camera moves. Give reactions and meaningful actions room to read. For HTML, compatible options include restrained parallax with reduced-motion support, accessible tap-driven character poses, reversible door-and-bloom reveals, bounded pupil tracking, and scroll-driven chapter/story states. These are optional, scene-dependent patterns. Video must derive states from seekable composition time; do not rely on live input. Keep one owner per animated property and make reverse/direct seeks coherent.
audio: Unspecified as a fixed style rule. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience; honor supplied audio choices. Support reading holds and motion cadence, leave space for speech, and verify intelligibility, balance, clipping, and synchronization.
assetRequirements: Prepare consistent character and background assets in narrative layers, with preserved transparency, stable dimensions, and clear naming. Layered PNGs or numbered frames can support composition; inspect them before use. Rigged poses need appropriate layers or a rig; gaze needs readable eyes. Paper texture, authored poses, and painted character details are not supplied by the suggested rendering libraries.
combinations: Works alone for picture-book narratives. Style-101 parallax backgrounds can add restrained environment depth; style-091 rigged poses can support reusable character acting. Keep warm palette, drawn edges, texture, occlusion, proportions, and reading clarity consistent. Avoid excess depth or camera speed. These are suggestions, not requirements.
productionApproach: Canvas 2D is the primary suggested style renderer; PixiJS can composite many 2D sprites, while Rough.js is optional for seeded sketch contours or hachure, not authentic painting, paper texture, handwriting, or character poses. Choose visual and motion tools for fidelity and action first. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, synchronization, validation, and export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, and record why. Keep rendering and motion logic in their own layers, drive video from deterministic seekable time, and inspect representative frames and the full export.
